blocks.costs: the weights are quantized at every start; below compute capability 8.9 (T4, A10G) only the stored weights shrink, so prompt processing is no faster
blocks.name: fp8-weights
blocks.reason: highest sampled KV-cache usage 92%; vLLM can store the weights in 8-bit fp8 when it starts, so each decode step reads half the weight bytes and the freed memory holds more requests (on this GPU the maths runs in 8 bits too)

blocks.costs: a different checkpoint, which Tensward does not download: register it with `tensward init --project <new> --model <its directory>` (same --config and --prompts), then `tensward analyse --project <new> --baseline-answers <this run>/responses.jsonl` shows its answers next to this run's
blocks.name: quantized-checkpoint
blocks.reason: highest sampled KV-cache usage 92%; a pre-quantized copy of this model runs on this GPU (compute capability 8.9). 8-bit: int8 W8A8, fp8 (W8A8). 4-bit, where answers change more often: AWQ int4, GPTQ int4, W4A16. int8 W8A8 and fp8 also run prompt processing in 8-bit arithmetic here

blocks.costs: TPOT rises when answers do not copy the prompt, and at high concurrency; a slower start
blocks.name: ngram-speculation
blocks.reason: prompts are long (median 495 words beyond what they share). N-gram speculation drafts tokens by copying spans of the prompt, so it only helps when answers quote or repeat their input; otherwise it costs a little - compare TPOT with and without it. Replaying prompt lookup on this run's answers, drafts would supply 9.2% of all output tokens; measure it: the step overhead on this model is not known
blocks.test: about 11 min on this setup (this run: 398 s to load, a 60 s window planned)

blocks.text: `trim-max-context-len`: vLLM gives the KV cache the memory left after loading the model whatever max_context_len is, and a request takes blocks only as it grows; trimming it adds no room and only refuses longer requests
